title: Datum · Brett Boggs
description: One system for running a construction company.

hero.heading: Datum

statement.heading: The office and the field, finally in one place.
statement.text: Construction runs on handoffs, and handoffs are where things get lost. Datum keeps the projects, the people, the equipment, the safety paperwork, and the money in one place, so nothing has to survive being passed between five different tools.

field.heading: Built for boots on the ground.
field.text: The field isn't an afterthought here. Daily reports, hazards, timecards, concrete pours. It all gets captured on site, while it's happening.

notes.text: Tenant isolation is enforced at the query layer rather than trusted to callers, with role based access through Entra ID. The agent layer runs inside that same boundary: a tool registry and persistent memory fenced by SQL guardrails and data policy, so an agent cannot reach across tenants.

An ERP adapter framework with a durable writeback queue, normalizing phase codes and cost types, so the platform talks to the accounting systems contractors already run. GDPR deletion and data subject export, which meant resolving one person across three identity systems that had never been connected.
A React Native app through TestFlight, an Outlook add-in deployed across the organization, and CI/CD into Azure with health checks and uptime monitoring.

system.heading: How it is put together
system.note: A request passes down through these layers. Rest on a plate, or tap one, and it explains itself. Nothing here is a number the page does not already count.
system.insideLabel: one tenant boundary, three layers deep

nodes.name: Web app
nodes.text: React. Everyone opens Datum to their own work: what needs action, what is coming up, and what is running late.

nodes.name: Field app
nodes.text: Daily reports, hazards, timecards and concrete pours, captured on site while they are happening.

nodes.name: Outlook add-in
nodes.text: An add-in deployed across the organization, so the office side of the work reaches Datum without leaving the mailbox.

nodes.name: Entra ID
nodes.text: Every request carries the tenant and the role of a principal the directory has verified. Nothing about either is taken from the caller, and later, nothing is taken from a model.

nodes.name: 338 services
nodes.text: Every handler runs inside a tenant scope and the pool primes that context on every query, so a call site cannot forget it. Twenty-nine background timers are wrapped the same way.

nodes.name: 132 SOPs
nodes.text: Standard operating procedures, automated end to end.

nodes.name: Agent layer
nodes.text: Agents run from a registry with per-agent tool grants and persistent, tenant-scoped memory. An agent inherits the clearance of the person asking and never has one of its own.

nodes.name: SQL guard
nodes.text: Model-authored SQL is proven read-only and tenant-bound in code, never in the prompt. Unknown tables count as tenant-keyed, so a table added tomorrow is protected before anyone updates a list.

nodes.name: Data policy
nodes.text: A foreman asking a colleague’s salary is refused, the way he would be at the HR office. Craft rates stay open to anyone who prices work.

nodes.name: Spend and kill switch
nodes.text: A per-tenant kill switch, a monthly spend cap and role gating, enforced where background jobs cannot go around them. Every statement runs with a five second lock timeout, because a foreman may be waiting on that row.

nodes.name: Azure SQL
nodes.text: One shared platform. Tenant columns are NOT NULL with no default, so an unstamped insert refuses instead of quietly landing in someone else’s company.

nodes.name: Row-level security
nodes.text: FILTER and BLOCK policies keyed to session context. A query that never set its tenant sees zero rows and writes none, however clever the SQL above it.

nodes.name: Tenancy lint
nodes.text: Any new table that has not declared its tenancy fails the build. It caught an unregistered table within weeks, with no human memory involved.

nodes.name: ERP adapter
nodes.text: The accounting system contractors already run owns actuals; Datum owns creation, estimates and projections. Verified intents queue in SQL with backoff, idempotent enqueue and an append-only sync log. Phase codes and cost types normalize per tenant.

nodes.name: GDPR
nodes.text: Deletion and data subject export, which meant resolving one person across three identity systems that had never been connected.

nodes.name: Azure CI/CD
nodes.text: Release into Azure with health checks and uptime monitoring.
